learningObjectives: Identify relevant and redundant features in a dataset.
Apply feature selection techniques to reduce unnecessary variables.
Explain how PCA reduces dimensionality while preserving important information.

activities.title: Feature Relevance Map
activities.instruction: Identify which features are relevant, irrelevant, or redundant for prediction.

content.concept: Relevant features provide useful predictive information, irrelevant features add little value, and redundant features duplicate information already captured by other variables.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Can provide useful information for predicting customer behavior.
Usually identifies a record rather than providing predictive information.
Can be strongly related to customer activity and predictions.
Contains information already represented by another income feature.

activities.title: Selection Strategy
activities.instruction: Match each feature selection approach to how it selects features.

content.concept: Filter methods evaluate features independently of a model, wrapper methods evaluate feature subsets using a model, and embedded methods select features during model training.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: Filter Method → Select features using statistical properties before model training
Wrapper Method → Evaluate different feature subsets using a model
Embedded Method → Select features as part of model training
Correlation Filtering → Remove highly redundant numerical features
config.answer: Filter Method → Select features using statistical properties before model training

activities.title: PCA Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the main stages of Principal Component Analysis.

content.concept: PCA transforms correlated features into a smaller set of principal components that capture important variation in the data.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Put numerical features on comparable scales when required.
Find new directions that capture variation in the data.
Determine how much variance each component explains.
Keep a smaller number of components based on the desired information retention.
Represent the original data using the selected components.

activities.title: Variance Slider
activities.instruction: Adjust the number of retained components and observe the trade-off between dimensionality and explained variance.

content.concept: Selecting more principal components generally retains more information but provides less dimensionality reduction.
